REWARD_MACHINE:
STATES: u0, u1, u2, u3
INITIAL_STATE: u0
FINAL_STATES: u3
TRANSITION_FUNCTION:
(u0, holding_box) -> u1
(u0, at_exit) -> u2
(u0, else) -> u0
(u1, box_fell) -> u2
(u1, at_exit & holding_box) -> u3
(u1, else) -> u1
(u2, holding_box) -> u1
(u2, at_exit) -> u2
(u2, else) -> u2
(u3, else) -> u3
REWARD_FUNCTION:
(u0, holding_box, u1) -> 0.2
(u0, at_exit, u2) -> 0.3
(u1, box_fell, u2) -> -0.3
(u1, at_exit & holding_box, u3) -> 1.0
(u2, holding_box, u1) -> 0.25
(u2, at_exit, u2) -> -0.1
feedback: The RM has serious fidelity and safety problems. (1) State u2 is reached via box_fell from u1 and via at_exit without the box from u0, but the transition (u2, holding_box) -> u1 rewards +0.25, so an agent can farm reward by repeatedly entering u2 (e.g., via exit without box, then picking the box up, dropping, re-entering) — or worse, u2 conflates two very different situations (lost box vs. at exit without box), so a single recovery reward is semantically wrong. (2) The at_exit self-loop in u2 pays -0.1 per step indefinitely (u2, at_exit, u2) -> -0.1; at_exit is a last-step-only condition, but if the episode ends this is a one-shot penalty, fine — yet if at_exit fires while the episode is truncated at the limit, the loop also rewards -0.1, small but unbounded density without progress. More importantly, (2a) the terminal requirement 'box in hands at exit' is only rewarded on the direct u1->u3 transition; an agent that reaches exit while holding the box after never dropping it never fires box_fell, so u1->u3 works — but an agent that picked up, dropped, and re-picked up (holding_box true again) while in u1 is fine; however the path u0->u2 (exit without box) then picking up the box and exiting gives no terminal reward path back to u3: from u2 -> u1 via holding_box, then u1 -> u3 via at_exit & holding_box, but the episode ends at exit so this is unreachable in practice; fine. (3) The core task requirement — 'if the box falls, pick it up again on your very next move' — is NOT encoded: the transition u1 --box_fell--> u2 with only -0.3 imposes no urgency and no enforcement that the very next step re-picks the box. A fall followed by a delayed pickup (many steps later) traverses the same transitions with the same rewards, so the RM cannot distinguish timely from late recovery; a per-step time penalty or an explicit intermediate 'fell, not yet re-picked' state with per-step penalty and a one-step deadline is needed. (4) Regression semantics: after re-picking from u2 -> u1, the +0.25 reward plus the possible cycle u1 -> u2 -> u1 via box_fell/holding_box means repeated fall-and-repick cycles yield -0.05 net per cycle and can be cycled indefinitely — reward is not bounded away from exploitability across an episode if falls can be triggered multiple times (second fall exists in half the episodes); dense progress rewards must be one-shot or strictly decreasing to prevent farming. (5) Also (u0, at_exit) -> u2 paying +0.3 rewards reaching the exit WITHOUT the box, directly contradicting the task (exit without box should pay 0); a smart agent collects 0.3 at u2 then the episode ends with the box task unfulfilled. Suggested fixes: separate u2 into 'fell' and 'at exit without box' states, remove or make negative the u0->u2 exit reward, add per-step time pressure while in the fell state with a strict one-step re-pick deadline, and make the re-pick reward non-repeatable (e.g., budget-style decreasing rewards) so cycles cannot be farmed.

(u2, else) -> u2
(u4, else) -> u4
(u3, else) -> u3
REWARD_FUNCTION:
(u0, holding_box, u1) -> 0.2
(u1, box_fell, u2) -> -0.05
(u2, holding_box, u1) -> 0.1
(u1, at_exit, u3) -> 1.0
(u0, at_exit, u4) -> 0.0
(u2, at_exit, u4) -> 0.0
feedback: The RM faithfully captures the task. Format is correct: nonempty FINAL_STATES with u3, all states declared, accepting final state. Transitions cover the required behavior: pickup in u0 (u0->u1, +0.2), exit with box held to accepting u3 (+1.0), exit without box in u0 or after a fall in u2 goes to sink u4 with 0 reward — correctly denying credit when the box is not held at the exit. Fall handling matches 'pick it up again on your very next move': a fall in u1 moves to u2 with -0.05 penalty, and repickup u2->u1 gives +0.1, so prompt recovery is encouraged (net +0.05) while lingering in u2 gains nothing. The else self-loops cover all irrelevant/unknown events (switch_toggled, siren_ringing, box_fell outside u1, holding_box where unlisted), satisfying per-state else coverage. Event predicates only, no derived conditions invented; box_fell and holding_box never co-occur so the event/condition distinction is safe. Rewards are bounded (max 1.0 at the exit) and the dense shaping (0.2 pickup, 0.1 repickup, small fall penalty) is bounded and monotone toward the goal. Note the -0.05 fall penalty is a mild shaping choice, not a task requirement; regression is explicit via u1->u2. Minor observation: in u1 the else loop retains holding_box, and a drop (holding_box becoming false) also self-loops in u1 — acceptable since a dropped box can be re-picked via the u0/u1 pickup... actually the u1 else self-loop keeps the agent in u1 after dropping, allowing re-pickup of a second box semantics — but since only one box exists and a re-pickup is not a new transition event, this is harmless and the fall/repickup path remains reachable. A second fall (after re-drop/re-pickup) would not re-enter u2 from u1, but that scenario requires a drop and the task's conditions are still met correctly at the exit. Accepted.
